item.title: Week 2 NFL live updates, schedule, inactives: Nico Collins, Zay Flowers ruled out; Brock Bowers doubtful, Joe Burrow questionable for Sunday
item.description: Follow along with all of the action on Sunday in Week 2 of the NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Week 2 of the NFL season continues with another slate of action Sunday afternoon — which fantasy football managers will, undoubtedly, hope follows the trend of offensive explosion showcased in Week 1. The league tied the post-merger record for the most Week 1 points scored ever at 791 across 16 NFL games.

Among the key injuries to know heading into Week 2: Texans wideout Nico Collins showed up on the injury report with a hamstring injury this week and was officially ruled out for Week 2, along with Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring). Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (rib) is questionable, while Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) was listed as doubtful.

On the quarterback front, Bengals star Joe Burrow is dealing with back tightness and was officially listed as questionable against the Bucs. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is dealing with a concussion suffered in Week 1 and was already ruled out, with veteran Carson Wentz set to start in his place. Seahawks' Sam Darnold was also already ruled out against the Cardinals (though he's avoided IR for now), with Drew Lock set to make his first start since 2024. Cooper Rush will again start for the Falcons in Week 2, with Tua Tagovailoa (back) doubtful and Michael Penix Jr. ruled out.

On a positive note, fantasy football managers will see New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson make his season debut returning from a preseason ankle injury.

item.title: Sam Darnold is "recovering faster than anyone had anticipated"
item.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the Week 1 game against the Patriots after five snaps, with a hip injury becoming a glute tendon injury for which the team reportedly sought multiple second opinions.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the Week 1 game against the Patriots after five snaps, with a hip injury becoming a glute tendon injury for which the team reportedly sought multiple second opinions.

Amid initial concerns that Darnold could miss 4-6 weeks, he could be back three weeks after the injury happened.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports that Darnold is "recovering faster than anyone had anticipated," and that he could return to practice "in some form or fashion" this week. That doesn't mean he'll be ready to go against the Commanders in Week 3. He could be back in Week 4 vs. the Chargers.

A significant game is looming in Week 5. That's when the 49ers, who beat the Seahawks in Seattle last season, return to town for what will be a potentially massive NFC West showdown.

Today against the Cardinals, it's Drew Lock. The Seahawks have beaten Arizona nine straight times, tying the longest active streak by any franchise against another team. Via NBC Sports research, the Chiefs have also beaten the Commanders nine straight times.

More importantly, the Seahawks have now won 11 in a row. That equals the longest streak in franchise history. Which means, obviously, that a win today would give Seattle its first-ever 12-game win streak.

item.title: Report: Michael Penix Jr. could debut for Falcons on Thursday night
item.description: The Falcons have been waiting.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons have been waiting. And waiting. And waiting.

The waiting may be over.

ESPN reports that quarterback Michael Penix Jr. "is nearing a return" and "could" make his 2026 debut on Thursday night, when the Falcons travel to Lambeau Field for a Week 3 contest.

During NFL Network's GameDay morning, Steve Wyche reported that Falcons president of football Matt Ryan said Penix is "getting close," but he declined to put a timetable on his return.

The team has had some muted frustrations about Penix's unwillingness to play. But he's not yet comfortable exposing his surgically repaired left knee to contact.

Without Penix, and with Tua Tagovailoa out due to an oblique injury, Cooper Rush started in Week 1, and he'll start in Week 2.

Through two seasons, Penix has 14 regular-season appearances and 12 starts, with four wins. After starting last season 3-2, Penix has lost four straight starts.

For now, the Falcons and Rush will face the Panthers, who won the division on the final Sunday of the 2025 season when Kirk Cousins led Atlanta to a win over the Saints.

item.title: Michael Penix could be the Falcons’ starting QB as soon as this Thursday night against the Packers
item.description: Atlanta’s wild ride at the quarterback position may soon be over. Michael Penix Jr. could take over as the Falcons’ starting QB in Week 3 vs. the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
When will Michael Penix be ready to start? That’s the question that’s been on everyone’s minds since at least Day 1 of this year’s training camp. According to reports from national insiders, that day may be coming up very soon.

According to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, Penix is ‘nearing a return’ and could take over as Atlanta’s starting quarterback as early as this Thursday night against the Packers in Lambeau.

What’s that mean for the future of Tua Tagovailoa? For now, he’ll stay on the roster, according to Rapoport.

I didn’t think Penix was genuinely an option for this week, regardless of what Stefanski said Wednesday about all quarterbacks being on the table to start this week. I don’t see a world where Penix starts on a Sunday and takes his first full-speed contact just four days before the next game. It’s just not smart. Starting in Week 3 and having a week and a half to rest up and prepare for the Saints in Week 4 on Monday Night Football is the smart play if Penix really is ready to go.

People may be surprised by the reporting around Tua and the team’s plans to retain him for now, at least. The quarterback room has pretty good vibes with its current construction (even though it’s still wild to me that they’re carrying four quarterbacks on the active roster), and with both Penix and Tua’s injury histories, having enough backup is a must.

I’ll feel sorry about it after he got trotted out there against the Steelers last week with a bad back, but if the Falcons get to a point where they feel comfortable with Penix’s health and availability I could see them moving on from Cooper Rush. The team seems high on Jack Strand’s potential, which … same. I don’t think they can stash him on the practice squad and realistically expect to keep him.

This quarterback saga has been quite the ride, and I’m ready for this ride to be over. Here’s hoping Penix is able to take over as the starter for Week 3 and that he stays healthy through the season.

item.title: Keys before kickoff: Cowboys vs Commanders Week 2
item.description: What do you think is the most important thing for the Cowboys today?
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders will mix it up on Sunday. Here are four keys to the game.

Getting defensive

In case you missed it – the Cowboys rebuilt defense was miserable in their first week of action against the Giants. They were so bad that the vaunted offense for Dallas saw the field just twice in the second half. In a sport where five to seven drives per half is the norm, that’s just flat out unacceptable.

This week, it’s imperative that we see some sort of improvement from the Cowboys defense. For starters, can the edges be disciplined enough to stay home on the outside and not bite on play fake after play fake? If you thought Jaxson Dart cooked them, just wait until Jayden Daniels gets out on the edge. The most important key on defense this week will be limiting what Daniels can do on the ground.

The Cowboys will also need to figure out a way to get pressure on Daniels without sending extra blitzers. It’ll be a tall task considering the talent they currently have on the field. Donovan Ezeiruaku was the only player to somewhat adequately rush the passer, but still below average in the department with two pressures on 20 pass-rush snaps. The front as a unit ranked 28th in the NFL in pass rush win-rate for week one. That needs to change this week and the numbers back it up. Jayden Daniels struggles when you can clog the passing lanes and still apply pressure with just the front four. It remains to be seen if Dallas has the horses to accomplish this task.

Time to air it out?

The Cowboys will need to commence ‘Operation: Find Mike Sainristil’ as early as the first play from scrimmage. Sainristil finished as one of the lowest grades cornerbacks in the league week one. He gave up multiple key plays against the Eagles, including a 64-yard completion to Dontayvion Wicks and a touchdown where he was completely lost in space. Both the corner and coach Quinn said it was an effort problem more than a scheme issue. With the ability Dallas possesses on the outside with Lamb and Pickens, finding Sainristil will be paramount.

Win the middle of the field

This week, Washington will be without Frankie Luvu (groin) and Chig Okonkwo (hamstring). That means the Commanders lose their best off-ball linebacker and their most dangerous receiving tight end for this week’s matchup against the Cowboys.

After Luvu went out last week, Sonny Styles wore the green dot for the remainder of the game. We all saw the highlight play where the linebacker bulldozed Barkley on his way to a sack on Jalen Hurts. But Styles graded out at just an overall grade of 48.6 (PFF), a 29.2 tackling grade (two missed tackles), and a 135.4 passer rating allowed when targeted.

Leo Chenal, the other off-ball linebacker, didn’t fare much better with an overall grade of 55.0 and a notable 31.5 tackling grade. His worst play of the day was a missed tackle on a 42-yard Barkley run. Chenal has elite athleticism but has historically struggled in coverage. He is more of a downhill, physical box player and blitz specialist.

While Dallas should focus on testing the cornerbacks early on with CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy, attacking the linebackers with Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford could be equally as important. Should Dallas choose to get their tight ends involved this week, they will likely find success in the middle of the field.

On the Cowboys defensive side, Washington has no proven pass catching threat at the tight end position after the loss of Okonkwo. That’s great news for a team that struggled last week to defend against an athletic pass catching tight end in Isaiah Likely. Forcing the Commanders to try and beat you on the outside with Stefon Diggs, Terry McLaurin and Antonio Williams without a safety blanket for Daniels at tight end will be a net positive for the Cowboys.

Turnovers

Against the Giants, the Cowboys had five turnover-worthy plays. They forced four fumbles and had a legitimate shot at one interception. Unfortunately, the interception that hit Durant in the stomach fell to the ground. Three of the forced fumbles were instantly magnetized to Giants players. In a sport where the oblong ball bounces in strange directions, it certainly did not bounce in the Cowboys favor.

If Dallas can once again focus on punch outs and force Daniels into making mistakes, they must capitalize on those gifts. Any extra possession that they can give this offense could be the difference in winning and losing. If the defense finds themselves struggling in a similar manner to week one, forcing turnovers would be a great equalizer.

item.title: These five Washington Commanders must dominate to beat Dallas Cowboys in Week 2
item.description: Count Terry McLaurin among those the Commanders needs to perform well to beat the Dallas Cowboys
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders and Cowboys face off on Sunday afternoon. For the (checks notes) 133rd time. Rarely do these matchups come so early in the season.  

Honestly, it’s kind of a bummer that the first contest falls in Week 2, but the Commanders were dealt this hand and simply must play it well. They can’t lose their second straight NFC East game in as many weeks.  

That would create a huge hole with lots of digging required to get out. That’s why the Commanders must play well and come away with a victory in Week 2.  

An 0-2 record is no fun. An 0-2 division record is even worse. They’ll need excellence from several key players to leave Dallas with a win. Here are five (not named Jayden Daniels) that must show up big for Washington:  

WR Terry McLaurin 

The veteran No. 1 receiver wasn’t a big part of Washington’s offense against Philadelphia. He wasn’t targeted until the fourth quarter, as the Eagles did a bunch to take him away. Washington still went to him in key moments late in that game, but he rolled with the punches like a veteran should.

Still, designing plays to get him involved early on Sunday could assist with McLaurin finding a required early flow.  

There should be room for him to work within the suspect Dallas secondary, and that connection he and quarterback Jayden Daniels refined all spring and summer must show up in important, explosive moments. It’s hard to keep McLaurin down. Seems borderline impossible in consecutive weeks.  

RB Bill Croskey-Merritt 

The team’s top running back led the Commanders with 63 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. While there were some hard runs in there, it’s still just 3.9 yards per clip. He’s got to be more efficient running the football in a zone scheme that suits him, but that’s not the most important thing.  

Hold onto the freaking ball.  

Croskey-Merritt got the ball punched out with roughly four minutes left in the fourth quarterback. That simply can’t happen. The Commanders acknowledged that point with actions, putting Kaytron Allen in the mix on that key comeback attempt.  

That was a shot across the bow if there ever was one.  

“Yeah, I think the ball security,” Quinn said, “that’s definitely the premium for us.” 

Croskey-Merritt must act like a feature back on Sunday, holding onto the ball while being a steadily productive force. If not, snaps may start going to others.  

LB Leo Chenal  

The Commanders will play Sunday without captain and green-dot wearer Frankie Luvu. That means Leo Chenal will step in and take most every snap next to Sonny Styles. Washington paid him handsomely to be a key defensive component.  

Chenal was more of a key reserve and roving chess piece in Kansas City, but he must be an every-down, stabilizing force in this one. There’s no second option with Jordan Magee on injured reserve, so Chenal has to be good in coverage, a stout run defender while shutting down plays before they turn explosive. That doesn’t sound super glamorous, but it’s a required job with Luvu unavailable.  

EDGE Dorance Armstrong 

The Commanders pass rush got off to a relatively strong start in Week 1, with impactful play when blitzing or applying a four-man rush. Now Washington adds Dorance Armstrong to the mix upon his reinstatement from a one-game suspension.  

Armstrong’s return from suspension and an ACL tear that cut an excellent start to the 2025 campaign short comes in Dallas, where the Texas native got hurt. It’s a full-circle moment to be sure, and he joins Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson as edge rushers.  

Quinn not-so-subtly hinted at the fact Armstrong could join those two in a personnel package that has all of them rushing the passer at once. Armstrong can bring it from the interior, too, and should make the Commanders four-man rush super dangerous.  

CB Mike Sainristil 

Have you reached Mikey fatigue at this point? The cornerback’s Week 1 gaffes have been rehashed and written about a ton in recent days, to the point its put-up-or-shut-up time. There isn’t much more to say other than that he’s got to play better, and has a tough task ahead against the Cowboys receivers.  

Commanders fans should keep an eye on his play and his usage in this one, to see if Washington’s staff sticks with Sainristil or decreases his snaps some. He’ll still be involved in that game in some capacity, and simply can’t give up the explosives that proved so costly in Week 1.

item.title: Dolphins fan confidence dips, concerns mount heading into Week 2 vs. 49ers
item.description: Miami Dolphins fan confidence dips after Week 1 while pass rush concern grows.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins struggled in all three aspects of their game against the Las Vegas Raiders, faltering on offense, laboring on defense, and getting gashed by long special-teams returns. It was not an ideal start to the season.

This season is not about wins and losses, though. This year’s focus is on the team developing the younger players and building toward the future. Miami is rebuilding, turning over much of the roster as a new front office and coaching staff put their stamp on the team.

Things may not get better this week as the Dolphins visit the San Francisco 49ers. According to the latest FanDuel Sportsbook odds, the Dolphins are 13.5-point underdogs. Not a lot is expected of Miami later today.

Fans concerned about lack of pass rush

The Raiders’ offensive line struggled to protect the quarterback in 2025. Last week, Miami could not get near Kirk Cousins. The pass rush simply never materialized. Now, the fans see it as the biggest area of concern with the team.

Out SB Nation Reacts poll for this week asked for where the concerns were for the Dolphins moving forward, and the fans zeroed in on the pass rush – and this is before the team’s top rusher, Chop Robinson, was ruled out of today’s game with a concussion – with 42 percent of the responses expecting more from the group.

The offensive line received 20 percent of the votes, special teams 13 percent, and the cornerbacks 4 percent. The remaining 22 percent voted “other.” Discussion around the poll included concerns about offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, penalties, and fans turning on the team and not giving the rebuild the time it needs to turn the franchise around.

Dolphins fan confidence

The Dolphins’ struggles against the Raiders were not unexpected, but it was still a rough game to watch. Our weekly fan confidence poll reflects the fan conflict between wanting to watch a competitive team putting up wins and the understanding that the team is resetting this year and building for the future. Last week, 79 percent of the fan base said they were positive about the team’s direction.

With the loss to the Raiders now on the board, our fan confidence poll dipped, but maybe not as much as a loss like that would have last year. According to our Week 2 survey, 63 percent of the fans are still supportive of the direction Miami is taking.

Miami Dolphins 2026 Season Fan Confidence Results:

Preseason – 80%
Week 1 – 79%
Week 2 – 63%

National Poll: Worst quarterback situation in league

This week’s SB Nation Reacts National survey included a question about the worst quarterback situations in the league. The Dolphins showed up in the results, but were nowhere near the top. Miami received six percent of the vote, more than the Minnesota Vikings (five percent) and the New England Patriots (two percent).

The Cleveland Browns dominated the results, receiving 67 percent of the vote. DeShaun Watson is starting for Cleveland, though he does not look comfortable, with Shedeur Sanders and Taylen Green backing him up. Dillon Gabriel is on injured reserve.

The Atlanta Falcons, who have a quarterback room that includes former Dolphins starting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa along with Michael Penix, Jr., Cooper Rush, and Nick Muse, picked up 19 percent of the votes, landing them in second place. Tagovailoa was expected to start the season at the top of the depth chart, but he missed the opener with an oblique injury and is doubtful for today.

item.title: Broncos are expected to be without RJ Harvey on Sunday
item.description: The Broncos are on track to be without one of their running backs for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos are on track to be without one of their running backs for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that RJ Harvey is not expected to play in Week 2. Harvey missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable after a pair of limited practices to close out the week.

Harvey had three carries for 18 yards and four catches for 23 yards in Denver's Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.

J.K. Dobbins is the top back for the Broncos with rookie Jonah Coleman and Tyler Badie set to move up the depth chart in Harvey's absence.

item.title: Report: Joey Porter Jr. considering second opinion on back injury
item.description: Porter will miss his second straight game on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will miss his second straight game on Sunday and his outlook for Week 3 remains uncertain as well.

The plan was for Porter to ramp up his workload this week, but he had to leave practice early on Thursday after his back flared up and he was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots. Porter is also working on his conditioning after spending all of training camp on the physically unable to perform list.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Steelers are targeting Week 3's game against the Bengals for his 2026 debut, but that Porter is considering a second opinion on his back. All of this is playing out against the backdrop of Porter's desire for a new contract that the Steelers aren't expected to discuss given their longstanding policy of not negotiating during the season.

That impasse has led to speculation about a trade, although nothing appears imminent with Week 2 about to get underway. Should Porter remain out as the trade deadline draws closer, things could change on that front.

item.title: Sunday Browns rumor: Shedeur Sanders’ time? Deshaun Watson’s final game?
item.description: According to a reported rumor, the Cleveland Browns will evaluate their QB competition again. Shedeur Sanders time?
item.content:encoded:
For Cleveland Browns fans, QB Deshaun Watson’s resume was full and faulty long before HC Todd Monken came in and gave everyone a clean slate. Almost no one was happy when Monken named Watson the Browns Week 1 starter, but the head coach has time and time again reinforced that he believes that decision is the right one for Cleveland.

Then in Week 1, the Browns offense was putrid with Watson as the quarterback, with some game-breaking issues, but Monken was steadfast that Watson was his starter. The veteran QB blamed the media, and the head coach backtracked on whether the team’s opinion mattered.

As we shared in this morning’s news wrap-up, our Daily Dawg Chow, there was a quick change in narrative around the quarterback position from Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com. Talking about Shedeur Sanders’ expectations and the possibility of a quarterback change after Week 2.

Then, Sunday morning brought this report of a rumor from ESPN and The NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport:

Rapoport noted that with Week 1’s bad loss and Cleveland having back-to-back road games, “the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point.”

Given this report, it is likely that a bad game from Watson would see Sanders as the starter for the home opener, and could spell the end of Watson’s NFL career. If the veteran plays well, especially with an upset victory, Watson could stave off Sanders for a few more weeks.

As Rapoport noted, “The middle ground is the area where it’s less clear cut.”

To some extent, two games seem like a very short evaluation time for such an important decision. Would that timeline have been true if Sanders was named the starter to start the season? If Watson is benched and Dillon Gabriel returns from injured reserve, would the veteran Week 1 starter even dress for games the rest of the year? Would Taylen Green stay on the roster and be the emergency quarterback?

Lots of questions that need to be answered, starting with Watson’s performance Sunday in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Given this report by Rapoport and the column by Cabot, it seems like Browns fans might get what they have wanted for a long time: No more Watson at quarterback.

What will Sanders look like if/when he gets his shot? That is a question that might take a little time to answer.

item.title: Column: FSU’s stars shined against Alabama; it wasn’t nearly enough
item.description: FSU’s star power was present but greatly overpowered in Tuscaloosa
item.content:encoded:
It’s no state secret that this is a deeply flawed Florida State football roster.

Some questionable decisions in how the money was divvied up, both positionally and in which players were brought in or retained.

But the roster has some bright spots, most notably at the offensive skill positions.

Say what you will about the quarterback, the offensive line, or the defense, there are some winning running backs and wide receivers on this year’s FSU team.

To have any chance at pulling off another upset of Alabama, the Seminoles were going to need standout games from those players.

As it turns out, they got them from pretty much all of them.

Duce Robinson was targeted eight times and had six catches for 135 yards — nearly double the 75 combined he had through the first two games — and his first score of the season.

Ousmane Kromah ran for 80 yards and another score, bringing his season totals to 311 yards and three scores in as many games.

Micahi Danzy (89 receiving yards) and Sam Singleton Jr. (68 receiving yards before leaving the game with an injury and using crutches to get back to the locker room) continued to showcase their playmaking ability.

They combined to spark FSU’s hot offensive start, which saw the Seminoles jump out to a 21-6 lead early in the second quarter and give just enough hope.

But even though they all delivered, it didn’t make a dent. The other holes on the roster were too big to overcome against Alabama.

The defense, which started with consecutive three-and-outs after managing just one in the first two games combined, allowed Alabama to score the next nine times it got the ball after that before it went into victory formation.

Ashton Daniels had a weird game that was both productive (his 377 passing yards were the most for FSU since the Wake Forest game in 2023) and far too mistake-prone (three interceptions).

While he amassed quite a few yards, I’m not sure I’d classify many of the throws he made as particularly tough. All in all, he largely looked like a quarterback not good enough to handle that stage or an opposing defense of that caliber.

His offensive line didn’t help Daniels in moments, but he also made matters worse at times by holding onto the ball far longer than was advisable in that setting.

That left a few very strong performances from FSU’s best players not amounting to much in the grand scheme of things.

And it leaves the Seminoles in a 1-2 hole, not likely to get much better with three more games in succession against teams that were ranked this week on the horizon after next week’s matchup with FCS Central Arkansas.

item.title: 49ers vs. Dolphins: How to watch, game time, and betting odds
item.description: Week 2 is upon us. The 49ers are back in the USA and ready to go for their home opener.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers play both their first game in Levi’s Stadium and their first game in North America for 2026 in Week 2. The 49ers have returned from Australia, where they beat the Los Angeles Rams, and jet lag is always a question, but it seems like the team has adjusted for Sunday’s game. This will be an afternoon game with Kevin Kugler on play-by-play and Daryl Johnston providing color.

Week 1 could not have gone any better for the 49ers. They went to the aforementioned Australia game and beat the Rams 27-7. It was a dominant 49ers performance and another great game for quarterback Brock Purdy. It wasn’t without some setbacks; wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling left the game and will be out for an extended period to have surgery, and tight end Jacob Tonges is out for the season. Besides those two, the 49ers are relatively healthy going into Week 2. Hopefully they can get through this game without any carts coming to the field.

The Dolphins aren’t positioned for anything grand in 2026. They’ve had a lot of churn in the offseason, some of the more notable moves being firing head coach Mike McDaniel and releasing quarterback Tua Tagovailoa. In the head coach’s seat is Jeff Hafley, former defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers. 49ers fans may remember Hafley as the team’s defensive backs coach from 2016 to 2018.

For quarterback, the Dolphins signed Malik Willis in the offseason. Week 1 was rough, with a 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Willis, in his first start as the Dolphins’ quarterback, went 15-of-27 for 220 yards passing, one rushing touchdown, an interception, a fumble, and took five sacks. The Dolphins’ rushing attack was equally disappointing, putting up just 74 yards total across 18 carries.

The Dolphins’ defense had a bit better day than the offense. While they recorded zero sacks, the secondary was decent, getting two interceptions and limiting Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins to 160 total yards passing.

The 49ers had a slight scare with kicker Eddie Pineiro not kicking due to an illness, but it’s been confirmed he will be playing. Running back Kaelon Black was also questionable, but it looks like he will be playing.

The Dolphins will be without EDGE Chop Robinson and inside linebacker Ronnie Harrison—both listed as out.

The 49ers are favored by nearly two touchdowns in this game. After what they showed us last week against the Rams, how they beat the Dolphins will be a discussion point rather than “if”. If the Dolphins can pull the upset or keep it within three points at the end of the game, that will not be a fun talking point on Monday.

item.title: Ultimate Fan: Last week’s reality check should serve Broncos well in home-opener
item.description: At least, it better.
item.content:encoded:
It’s hard to believe it only took until Week 2 for Broncos Country to hit the panic button! Just kidding. It’s not surprising at all. And I’ll be the first to admit being among them. Last week’s pretend football game was atrocious and I am officially a little worried.

But I’m not that worried because like our veteran Ultimate Fan, bill2975, points out: “They can’t be that bad two weeks in a row, can they?”

No, they can’t. Well, they better not be. And I don’t think they will. Last week’s wake-up call to players and coaches, combined with playing in front of the Mile High crowd, should make for a much better Week 2!

Week 2: Broncos v. Jaguars

MHR – I hardly know where to start with last week’s game, but after several days and a few deep breaths, it seems ok to just ask, WTF happened?
bill2975: Here’s what I posted after the Monday night game, “Reality check! The Broncos played a terrible game, so let’s do better next week.  Good thing it’s Game 1, so the coaches will certainly have the team’s attention now.  What the hell, we weren’t threatening the 1972 Dolphins, anyway.”

MHR – Bo Nix didn’t look “bad” in my opinion but certainly looked rusty. Was it first-game-back-from-injury jitters? Was it prime-time in Week 1? Was it the O-line? Was it Arrowhead? Was it a new play-caller? Was it being a new dad and not having enough sleep? Are you concerned or do you believe it was just a one-off and he’ll be back on track this Sunday?
bill2975: I hope the team got a good wakeup call after being humbled by a team they should have beaten, even if it was in a terrible place to play (KC – good BBQ but insufferable fans, aka zealots).  Hope the team focused on how to tackle this week; they apparently missed that session last week, and the coaching didn’t help much as they frequently seemed out of position.  Oh, hopefully McGlinchey plays better this week,which shouldn’t be difficult.

MHR – Depending how you answered the previous question, what was going on with the offensive line on Monday Night? Nix seemed to be running away from trouble most of the game. How does our O-line protect Nix this week from a Jags’ D-line that got five sacks in week 1 (it was against the Browns, but still…)?
bill2975:I’m not a football expert, but I wonder if trying to use the middle of the field on passes would have helped a lot.  Maybe we could try that THIS week?

MHR – Despite the promise of a better rushing attack, the Broncos once again failed “to establish the running game” (15 attempts for 61 yards, compared to 38 attempts by the Chiefs and 173 yards by KWIII alone!) Is this a failure of game planning or was it an issue with “taking what the defense gave us” and not having the right situation to run the ball? Or did we just get behind too early?
bill2975:I vote for game planning being much of the problem.  And not very many runs.  Maybe the first series or two they should run, run, run.  Hell, try the single wing offense, if necessary.  Show the Jags something they don’t know how to handle.  Maybe try the Eagles Tush Push approach every play until they stop it.

MHR –  Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton – WR1 and 2 – combined for…wait for it…3 catches for 13 yards. It seems like such an absurd stat I don’t even know what question to ask other than…why?
bill2975:Wasn’t Nix running for his life much of the time?  Try some quick, short passes over the middle after establishing the run game.

MHR – Moving to Denver’s defense where we usually ask fun questions about dominance, what in the living hell was that tackling on Monday Night? Or should I say, non-tackling? It’s the most fundamental part of playing defense and our guys looked like my grad-school flag football team. Do you expect them to be back on track this week? 
bill2975:See my comments above.  Maybe they planned a practice session on how to block and tackle, but didn’t get to the latter piece.  Good thing we weren’t flying to Australia and back.

MHR – Trevor Lawrence has had his ups and downs, but he has hung in there at Jacksonville and last year proved he has staying power in this league. What concerns you the most about him on Sunday? Can Nik Bonitto and Que Robinson and/or Jonah Elliss rattle him enough to keep from getting quick scores?
bill2975:Disclaimer – I’ve always liked Trevor Lawrence, and I expect him to be really good on Sunday.  Sure would be nice to see the edge rushers get close to him, though, and throw him off his game.

MHR – Like Denver, Jacksonville has a slew of decent running backs, but no superstar like KWIII (hopefully!) But Denver’s run defense is still a concern. How do they stop Tuten, Abdullah and Rodriquez – a trio that combined for 121 yards last week? 
bill2975:Is John Franklin Myers available this week?  Oh, you say he moved on?  Well, crap…

MHR – Looking at the Jacksonville receivers, Parker Washington had a field day against the Browns with 83 receiving yards while Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr. combined for another 80 yards. Will the defensive backs answer Pat Surtain’s call for better “intention” to tackle this weekend? How will our DBs stack up against their WRs?
bill2975:I’d be shocked if our DBs had a second bad game in a row on Sunday.  Linebackers, though?  Eh…

MHR – Our best player on Monday was Jeremy Crawshaw, the punter. Which one player/unit on both sides of the ball needs to have a great game this weekend to help the Broncos beat the Jags?
bill2975:Riley Moss and Ja’Quan McMillian.  I don’t worry very much about Pat.  And, Zach Allen’s friends on the DL have to try to make Trevor’s life miserable, too.  (Hm.. that’s more than one!)

MHR –  Aside from obviously coming away with a win, what would you most like to see from the team this week that would indicate progress and a promising season overall?
bill2975:Honestly, what I care about is seeing a well-played, well-fought, penalty-free game with several exciting plays.  I’d like to see a win, particularly in Denver, but let’s turn things around and get going in the right direction.

Predictions

Stats for BO NIX? Enough to win the game. 

Stats for each Broncos RB?  How about 4+ YPC or better for each one, and enough run plays to matter.

Number of yards receiving/TDs for each of the receivers?  I vote for at least 180 yards total.

How many points for Lutz this week?   3 PATs, 2 FGs.

Number of sacks to Trevor Lawrence? 3-4

Broncos player with the most tackles?  Sigh, Singleton, preferably at the line of scrimmage.  Maybe Murdock, if he’s playing.

Who gets the first sack of the game for the Broncos?  Bonitto.

Who gets the most sacks?   Bonitto, tie with Allen and Hufanga.

How many INTs/FF/FR for the Jaguars’ D?   None

How many INTs/FF/FR for the Broncos’ D?   More than None.

How many penalties between the two teams?   Way too fricking many!

The Favorites 

Favorite Broncos win ever? Demarius’ walkoff TD against Steelers

Favorite John Elway win outside of the Super Bowls?  “The Drive” – 1987

Favorite Peyton Manning win?  Broncos 49, Ravens 27; Peyton 7 TDs.  Vinovich revenge…

Team you love to beat the most in the AFC West?  Tie – Chefs, Faders, Charge-its

Coach you laugh at the most in the NFL?  Mike McDaniel

Coach you most want to throat punch? Joshua Thomas McDaniels, or maybe Belicheat (this is my Emeritus pick)

Team you hate to lose to the most in the rest of the AFC?  Cheatriots

NFC team you could cheer for in the Super Bowl? Buffalo Bills

NFC team you want to face more than any other in the Super Bowl? New Orleans Saints, with some good gumbo

Toughest game on the schedule? Seahawks

Favorite Broncos player on the current roster?  Zach Allen

Favorite Broncos player of all time not named John Elway (unless it really is John Elway)? Otis Armstrong (Purdue with me), and Omar Moreno

Favorite new guy/rookie on the team? Almost new – Pat Bryant

Food/Snack you have to eat on game day? Popcorn

Favorite game analyst/commentator? Hard to tell with the sound turned off…

Give me one word/phrase/cliche to describe your hope for this season?  Indomitable team

Who is on your Broncos’ Mount Rushmore?  Floyd Little, John Elway, Von Miller, Champ Bailey (might be different if you were to ask me again)

How did you become a Broncos fan?

I’ve said this here before. I met my future wife in Denver at a USO Dance (while attending a Navy school) back in the dawn of time, and was already a fan of the Broncos (probably because of Floyd Little, who I watched play in college at Syracuse, which is also the college home of RBs Jim Brown and Ernie Davis). It was only after we married that she accused me of making false pretenses – I can’t dance worth a crap. It’s taken many years, but she’s come to accept that.

I went to college at Purdue with Otis Armstrong, so that helped me cheer for the Broncos, too. I am usually objective and rational, though sometimes referred to as a crotchety curmudgeon, according to wife. 😎 Biggest disappointment was losing to the Ravens in the playoffs in 2013, in spite of Trindon Hollidays’s TDs.  I think that’s how my TV got broken…

I subscribe to NFL Gamepass each year to watch every Broncos game, plus any others

of interest, even though the NFL app and UI are pretty bad for something owned by zillionaires.  

And another rant about the Chefs – do we really have to see all these shots of Taylor in the owner’s box? I do admire Mahomes (though not the KC fan base trolls), even if he does resemble Kermit the Frog. 😎

item.title: New York Jets vs Green Bay Packers Pre-Game Ball
item.description: Who will be a key factor for the Jets against the Packers?
item.content:encoded:
We’re going to try something new here. Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. Let’s do something a little more difficult. Let’s hand out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on one player we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit.

One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. 

This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’ll probably get most of these wildly wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. So without further ado, let’s get to it.

The inaugural Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Green Bay Packers goes to (drum roll please) – Kenyon Sadiq.

This game might be a bit early for a Sadiq breakout. He missed virtually the entire offseason for the Jets and is still getting integrated into the offense. No matter. Go big or go home, right? Since I’m already home, I’m going big.

The Green Bay Packers have struggled recently defending against tight ends. Last week T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver combined for 6 receptions for 56 yards and a touchdown. Last year, in 18 games including the playoffs, the Packers gave up 105 receptions for 902 yards and six touchdowns to tight ends.

Against teams that featured better, more athletic tight ends, in nine games the Packers gave up a combined 57 receptions for 552 yards and four touchdowns. Those came against a combination of Sam LaPorta, David Njoku, Harold Fannin, Jake Ferguson, Tre McBride, Dallas Goedert, Mark Andrews, Isaiah Likely and Colston Loveland. Kenyon Sadiq has obviously not yet earned a place among the NFL’s best tight ends yet, but he is more athletic than any of those guys, and has the potential to swiftly rise up the ranks. Why not start the rising right now?

The Jets are down to just four wide receivers today. Two of the four, Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith, have yet to make an impact as NFL receivers. The Jets will likely respond to the lack of established targets at wide receiver with a bunch of heavy, multiple tight end sets. They showed last week they wanted to get Sadiq involved in a variety of ways early, despite his lack of practice reps. Why not make this Sadiq’s coming out party?

This is probably way too early for the rookie, but what the heck? Let’s have some fun. Kenyon Sadiq, come on down! Let’s see you light up the Packers on a dreary, rainy Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford. You get our first ever pre-game ball. Try not to drop it.

What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Giants expect Aaron Donald ‘to play like Aaron Donald’ in return to Rams
item.description: The Giants are expecting nothing less than Donald’s best on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald is expected to make his return to action on Monday for the Los Angeles Rams after a two-year retirement. So, what are the New York Giants expecting from the nine-time All-Pro and 10-time Pro Bowler?

They are expecting Donald, 35, to be the great player he was during his initial 10 years in the NFL.

“Expect him to play like Aaron Donald, which is a game-wrecking type player inside,” Giants head coach John Harbaugh said. “Penetrating, active movement player who can wreck the game, really any particular play in a lot of different ways, run and pass. So, we’re expecting him to play. We’re planning for him to be out there.”

Donald said this week that he is “feeling good”, and the “the plan” is for him to play.

Donald tried to downplay his potential impact, or the idea that he would get extra attention from Giants blockers.

“You think they’re going to double/triple team me [after] not playing for two years? They ain’t worried about me, man,” Donald said. “They don’t have to be worried about me. They don’t have to worry about me at all. No man, they don’t have to worry about me.

“Whatever happens, I’m just going to go out there and play my game and just try to do what I can do. I don’t know what they’re going to do out there. I don’t know what I’m going to get. All I can know is I got a game plan. I’m going to go out there, execute it, and just try to play ball. That’s it.”

The Giants will, of course, give etxra attention to one of the greatest defensive linemen of his generation.

Giants left guard Jon Runyan has played against Donald before. Runyan, rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa, and center John Michael Schmitz will have primary responsibility for containing Donald whenever he is on the field Monday night.

Runyan understands what Donald, even a rusty Donald, can do.

“He’s a really unique player for the defensive tackle position. He’s not the biggest guy, he’s listed as 6 foot, I don’t really know if he’s even 6 foot, 285, super strong, super athletic, super fast,” Runyan said. “He gets the ability to kind of play how he wants, jump around blocks, and he’s good at that.

“He’s out there to make plays. Great pass rusher, obviously. Very physical, strong, good with his hands, and he’s just on a different level when it comes to understanding, leverage, using his strengths, like his speed and his hands. He diagnoses everything really fast, and that’s why he’s been doing it at a high level for so long, and probably one of the best to do it of all time.”

Donald will likely play a limited number of snaps.

“I’ll probably be a lot more fresh. I’ll probably be fresh. It’s a long year, long season,” Donald said. “We have a lot of good football players out here. My game plan is, however it’s going to be, I’m going out go out there and play hard. And when I need a break, tap out, let the next guy go out there and eat, and I’ll be right back. I think we have a good game plan to get myself going and get this team going. Whatever that role is, I’m ready for it. I’m excited about it and I’m just going to do it.”

Quarterback Jaxson Dart has watched enough football, and looked at enough film, to understand the kind of player Donald has been.

“For the longest time that I can remember, he’s one of the most dominant players that I’ve watched,” Dart said. “So, getting the chance to go out there and compete against him, it’s going to be really cool just to be on the same field as him. He’s a great player, and I’ve heard that he’s kept himself in really good shape. So, it’s going to be a great competition.

“The real impact on the game from just a game plan standpoint, there’s countless clips of putting three offensive linemen on him and still being able to make a play. So, he’s an unbelievable player and has had an unbelievable career.”

Running back Cam Skattebo understands there will will likely come a time during the game where he meets Donald in the hole on a run play.

“I’m excited to play against him. He’s one of the best to ever do it. It’s going to be fun. It’s going to be a good challenge for the guys up front. It’s going to be a good challenge,” Skattebo said. “If I have to meet him in the hole on third and one, then so be it. I’ve got to get one yard. But he’s a good player. He’s one of the best to ever do it. So, all respect to him.”

The Seattle Seahawks (1-0) and Arizona Cardinals (1-0) came away with Week 1 wins against AFC opposition to start the 2026 season. Now these NFC West foes will begin their division slate in Glendale, with the home team riding high off an unexpected victory.

It was a successful start for Mike LaFleur as Cardinals head coach, leading Arizona to a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood. The Seahawks are hoping that their season will end with Super Bowl 61 in Inglewood, and the reigning champs overcame injury to Sam Darnold to win 13-10 over the New England Patriots. They will not have Darnold for this Cardinals game, and they will also be without safety Ty Okada and guard Anthony Bradford. It’s TBD on defensive back Nick Emmanwori, but limited practices all week indicate he won’t be available. Drew Lock will run the Seahawks offense in his first start for the team since 2023, and the good news is he’ll have wide receiver Tory Horton back from his hamstring injury.

The Seahawks defense locked down Drake Maye and the Patriots offense when it mattered most in Week 1, and now they’ll be tasked with slowing down Jacoby Brissett and his top target, tight end Trey McBride. This will also be a fascinating matchup of running backs, as Seattle’s Jadarian Price and Arizona’s Jeremiyah Love will feature in a battle of Notre Dame rookies. The former teammates will be foes on Sunday, and the Seahawks run defense has been almost impenetrable for almost two years.

item.title: Trey Hendrickson, Chris Olave, Chase Young are expected to play in Ravens-Saints
item.description: The Ravens will be without wide receiver Zay Flowers for Sunday's game against the Saints, but they are set to have linebacker Trey Hendrickson in the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens will be without wide receiver Zay Flowers for Sunday's game against the Saints, but they are set to have linebacker Trey Hendrickson in the lineup.

Hendrickson was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report of the week after returning to practice on Friday. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Hendrickson is expected to play while wearing a cast to protect his injured finger.

Flowers is out with a hamstring injury and the Saints' top wideout Chris Olave has also been dealing with a hamstring issue this week. Olave traveled with the team to Baltimore and Rapoport reports that Olave is set to play on Sunday.

Saints defensive end Chase Young, who has a calf injury, is also expected to play.

item.title: Eagles News: Philly fans are taking over Tennessee
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/20/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

No surprise here since we all know Eagles fans travel very well in general. But it seems like there’s an especially large presence in Tennessee given the destination and the fact that the Eagles haven’t played there since the 2018 season. Add in the Titans drawing dead and the Eagles having optimism for their season … and it should certainly be a home game for the Birds on the road once again.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

“We’re Gonna Own That Stadium” – Philadelphia Eagles Fan Are Taking Over Nashville Ahead Of Titans Game – Whiskey Riff

Just take it from Eagles super-fan Paul Edwards. He got stopped by the local news on his way from Philly to Nashville, and here’s what he had to say: “Let’s get this party started buddy. Here we go, here we go. Tennessee Titans? We’re gonna own that stadium. There’s no doubt about that. Get ready for a stompin’. Be ready for our offensive line to run you over. Go Birds!” Something tells me thousands upon thousands of “Pauls” will be at Nissan Stadium. Eagles fans appear to be getting to Nashville early to make the most of the weekend. There’s been plenty of videos of green-garbed Philadelphians walking around in Nashville and taking over bars on Broadway. They are even getting their “E-A-G-L-E-S EAGLES chants” going anywhere and everywhere they can.

The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the first time this season to take on the Tennessee Titans. Man, it’s (going to be) a hot one with a projected feels like temperature of 94 degrees Fahrenheit at Sunday’s 1:00 PM kickoff. In order to preview this Week 2 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Music City Miracles. Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation was nice enough to answer 5 questions about his Philadelphia Eagles ahead of tomorrow’s matchup. That day is not today.

NFL Week 2 betting primer: 15 games, trends and key numbers – The Athletic

Bad offense: Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, the Philadelphia Eagles featured five three-and-outs and only 10 first downs, far below the league average of 19.8 first downs in Week 1. More bad offense: The Tennessee Titans managed only 195 total yards in their home opener against the Jets, had just 194 yards in the 2025 season finale at Jacksonville and failed to break 200 total yards in three other games last year. Road warriors: Since Nick Sirianni took over in 2021, Philadelphia is 30-13 on the road, a near 70 percent win rate — the best in the NFL over that span.

Tennessee Titans team total UNDER 15.5 (-105). Philadelphia’s defensive front looked as deep and disruptive as ever against an average Washington Commanders front, and the Titans are comfortably one of the eight worst lines in football. Though defensive back Cooper DeJean was banged up in the Week 1 game and sat out practice Wednesday, the Eagles’ outside corner duo of Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen still poses a huge problem for the Titans’ ability to create explosive plays through the air. The talent difference here feels simply insurmountable. The Titans will need defensive takeaways or big special teams outputs to get into scoring range. I don’t see them getting enough. I would play this up to -115.

item.description: Steelers game picks for Week 2
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and New England Patriots will square off today in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Pittsburgh won this matchup last season by the score of 21-14 off the strength of five takeaways. Can they win consecutive matchups against New England and get to 2-0? Here is how our staff sees things playing out.

Ryan Parish (1-0): The Steelers won this matchup a year ago thanks to some turnover luck. I think they will need more of that as the Patriots were a much different team by the end of the season.Fortunately for Pittsburgh, the Patriots’ offense is in a bit of disarray and is shorthanded following the injury to A.J. Brown. The Pats do get TreVeyon Henderson back, but how effective will he be in his first game back? The Steelers’ offense will likely still be uneven, especially with wide receiver Michael Pittman out, but I think the defense can lead them to another ugly win. Steelers 20, Patriots 17

Ryland Bickley (1-0): I was leaning towards a Steelers win, but Michael Pittman Jr.’s sudden absence feels like a big deal after he was the team’s most consistent wide receiver last week. I’m confident Germie Bernard will step into a bigger role on offense some time this season, but after barely seeing the field last week, it might be too early to expect much –especially considering Aaron Rodgers’ demands of receivers. The Patriots are certainly a beatable team, especially with wide receiver AJ Brown out, but Drake Maye is a different class of quarterback from the Falcons’ Cooper Rush, who the Pittsburgh defense easily handled last week. It could be a different story Week 2. I’m expecting a close game that could go either way. Steelers 20, Patriots 17

Austin Bechtold(1-0): I’m concerned with the Steelers offensive line facing a more vaunted pass rush than the Falcons. Missing Michael Pittman Jr. should unlock playing time for Germie Bernard, but does Aaron Rodgers trust him? Does DK Metcalf bounce back?  Drake Maye can’t possibly be as bad as he was against the Steelers last year. New England might not be the house of horrors it used to be for the Steelers, but I think the Patriots do enough in the 4th quarter with multiple question marks surrounding the Steelers offense and its capabilities. The defense should force a turnover or two, but I don’t see it being enough and the absence of Joey Porter Jr. will be felt more than most of us think. Patriots 24, Steelers 21.

Mike Nicastro (1-0): The Steelers and Patriots rosters are comparable, but this is a tough spot for Pittsburgh in what feels like a must win for New England. After losing to Seattle on opening night, they risk falling to 0-2, prior to heading to play on the road at Jacksonville and Buffalo. The Steelers defense will most certainly keep them in the game, but ultimately Drake Maye will make too many plays with his legs. The potential absence of Michael Pittman Jr. looms large, as shutdown corner Christian Gonzalez will likely blanket DK Metcalf most of the game. For the Steelers to win, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard will need to have the games of their lives. It’s a tough spot in wet conditions. Patriots 20 Steelers 16.

Joey Bray (1-0): The Pittsburgh Steelers beat this same team in this same location last season. However, it’s hard to imagine the Steelers force five turnovers this time around against a very well coached New England team. The absence of key pass catchers should make offense harder to come by in his contest. Drake Maye will be without AJ Brown, while Aaron Rodgers will be without Michael Pittman Jr. I’ll take New England to get back on track and pick up a win at home. Patriots 17, Steelers 13.

Jason Aponte (1-0): Michael Pittman is down, but this feels like a perfect squeaky wheel game for DK Metcalf. Christian Gonzalez is a problem, but he’ll still be involved. The Patriots missing A.J. brown means more than anyone wants to let on. It’ll be ugly, but Pittsburgh goes 2-0. Steelers 21, Patriots 17.

Jarrett Bailey (1-0): I’ve gone back and forth on what I believe will happen here. No Michael Pittman means Roman Wilson and/or Germie Bernard need to step up. The Steelers also need to be able to have some semblance of a ground attack, which they didn’t have against the Falcons in Week 1. I picked the Patriots on the latest episode of The Pump Fake (shameless plug, join me and Todd Haley for three shows per week), so I’ll stick with that here, though I certainly do see a path where the Steelers prove me wrong. Patriots 24, Steelers 23.

Let us know what you think in the comments. Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

item.title: 5 questions and answers about Patriots vs. Steelers
item.description: We spoke with SB Nation’s Steelers blog about the Patriots’ upcoming opponent.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots return home on Sunday to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in their home opener. The game is a rematch from last year’s regular season, but there has been substantial change particularly for the Steelers since the two franchise’s last crossed paths in 2025.

In order to find out more about the Patriots’ Week 2 opponent, we spoke with Ryland Bickley of Pats Pulpit’s sister site Behind the Steel Curtain, the SB Nation community for all things Steelers.

What team-wide effect has Mike McCarthy thus far at head coach? How has his relationship with Aaron Rodgers evolved since the last time they were together?

After nearly 20 years under the CEO-like leadership of Mike Tomlin, a lot is different under McCarthy, from big, on-field changes to things as simple as no longer providing an injury report in a postgame opening statement.

Obviously, it’s still far too early in the new Mike’s tenure to make sweeping judgements on what has been different, but some things that have been noticeable include assistant coach hires such as Patrick Graham, who has been a breath of fresh air on defense (more on that later), and McCarthy being more hands-on in player development, notably at quarterback.

Of course, McCarthy is the Steelers’ offensive play caller, unlike Tomlin, and his offense has looked different from past Steelers teams even if it wasn’t reflected on the scoreboard last week. For starters, there’s already been a bigger emphasis on middle of the field passing, and the run game is more varied than Arthur Smith’s zone-heavy philosophy last year. 

As for the Rodgers/McCarthy relationship, I can’t speak too much to that as I’m not actually in the Steelers building. But while Rodgers is still no stranger to bizarre headlines, a common theme of his time with the Steelers has been teammates singing the praises of their veteran quarterback. He’s well-liked in that locker room and seems to only be playing because he still enjoys it. 

On the field, Rodgers did look a lot better than his 2025 self last week, pushing the ball downfield more and being willing to extend plays when needed. The big question this week is if that trend will continue, or if Week 1 was an outlier due to Rodgers facing an undermanned Falcons pass rush. 

The Steelers’ receivers missed out on some downfield opportunities last week. Are you concerned there may be a long-term issue, or was it just Week 1 rust?

Yes and no. Some Week 1 rust was always expected, especially as Rodgers has always been a quarterback who relies heavily on strong chemistry with his pass catchers. 

That said, despite being built like a jump-ball receiver, DK Metcalf plays more like a pure speed threat. Last week was an especially bad game for him, but his inability to come down with the ball on some tougher grabs wasn’t exactly a surprise, either. Still, he had a brutal, clean drop on an in-breaker that would’ve gone for a chunk play or even a score last week, and I’d expect him to make the catch in the future. 

Another interesting name is Roman Wilson, a third-round pick in 2024, who looks to be finally making an impact on offense this year as Pittsburgh’s WR3 to open the season. He and Rodgers almost connected on a few plays, but “almost” has been a common theme of Wilson’s NFL career thus far. To sum up my point, the Steelers’ offense showed some big-play potential last week, but it’s still hard to tell if that will actually lead to anything.

I’ll add that a pleasant surprise last week was Michael Pittman Jr., who’s hardly a burner at this point in his career, but showed off some good chemistry with Rodgers and a knack for finding soft spots in defenses for big gains. [Editor’s note: Pittman Jr. has been ruled out for the game]

Have the Steelers’ offensive line and secondary changes been a net positive or negative?

Not to sound like a broken record, but it’s still too early to tell. The offensive line had a rough preseason and some struggles against Atlanta last week, but first-round right tackle Max Iheanachor is still working his way into the lineup and top starters Troy Fautanu (left tackle) and Mason McCormick (left guard) have both switched from playing on the right side last year. That’s led to some understandable growing pains. 

The group has plenty of talent, especially with Zach Frazier remaining a stalwart at center, but the Patriots should be able to see some success against a weaker right side of the line. The run game was especially rough last week, with the Steelers averaging -1.14 yards before contact per carry — worst in the NFL.

As for the secondary, the cornerback room, with Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. starting on the outside, held up well against the Falcons last week despite the absence of Joey Porter Jr. (also not expected to suit up against New England). Jalen Ramsey has definitely lost a step but remains an above-average defender, playing in the slot in nickel defense and rotating to safety in base. Jaquan Brisker recorded an interception last week at safety and made an impact near the line of scrimmage. 

The problem, of course, is that the success came against Cooper Rush at quarterback; Drake Maye will be a much bigger issue. While the cornerback room is solid, there’s a real lack of range at safety the Patriots could definitely exploit, and the Steelers are already thin at the position with DeShon Elliott on injured reserve. 

How has Patrick Graham put his fingerprint on the Steelers’ defense? Do you think they stick to an all-zone approach vs Drake Maye?

Graham was running some hilariously complex sim pressures and coverages at times in the preseason, and actually simplified things once Week 1 hit. My take is that the Steelers realized they didn’t have to overcomplicate things to beat Cooper Rush last week, and guessed correctly. Instead, they sat back, let the defensive backs see things unfold in front of them in zone, and took advantage of some miscues on offense. 

Against the Patriots, I’d expect more varied coverages, but even against Atlanta, a lot of what was classified as zone was match coverages, which have a lot in common with man concepts. Graham does like to play a lot of split-safety coverages, with a heavy dose of cover 4 last week, and I’d expect that to continue in Week 2. 

Outside of the secondary, Graham is known for helping his inside linebackers succeed in his scheme, and that was on display in Week 1 with Payton Wilson playing one of the best games of his career after a rough 2025. The Steelers have a pair of highly-athletic off-ball linebackers in Wilson and Patrick Queen, and under Graham they’ve been looking a lot more comfortable. 

Do you anticipate more blitzing from the Steelers against Drake Maye? If not, how do you feel about their ability to affect the quarterback rushing on only four?

To parrot my above answer, the Steelers’ defensive game plan was very Falcons-specific last week, and I’d expect Graham to mix things up against New England. Graham himself said more blitzes would be coming when asked about it by the media earlier this week. 

Still, the Steelers are more capable than most teams at generating pressures with just four rushers. The team’s top three outside linebackers — T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig — are all fantastic players with varying skill sets, and Watt returned to form against the Falcons, winning the AFC Defensive Player of the Week award for Week 1. So far, Graham has done a great job rotating and finding unique usages for all three players, even giving Herbig some inside linebacker snaps at times against Atlanta. 

Inside, Cam Heyward remains a force in his late 30s with a lethal bull rush. The recently-extended Keeanu Benton has a potent club move and has been growing as a pass rusher, with a career-best 5.5 sacks last season.

item.content:encoded:
It’s game day in the Mile High City where the Denver Broncos hope to course correct in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars after an embarrassing defeat in opening weekend. The series is all tied up at 8-8 including playoffs with the Jaguars smoking the Broncos last year in Denver, 34-20. Before that, though, the Broncos had won four of five going back to 2016. Oddly enough, the Broncos have not beaten Jacksonville in their home stadium since 2013.

Game preview

There are two big questions heading into this game for the Broncos. The first will be on defense. Can they actually tackle? If they had tackled well, they would have been the most dominant defense in the NFL last week as they led in first contact on run plays and shut Patrick Mahomes all the way down in the passing game. So maybe if they start tackling again, we won’t have much to complain about on defense.

The other question comes to Bo Nix. He had a terrible game all the around. We lit up Davis Webb, but Nix left a lot of big plays on the field by turtling up after that early interception. We’ll need to see a lot more confidence from him in Week 2 and Webb needs to commit to the run game a little earlier in this game.

If both of those questions get answered with a positive for Denver, then I think they actually win this game despite the Jaguars being a pretty good team in 2026.

item.title: Panthers vs Falcons: Round table predictions, odds, and Atlanta Bryce
item.description: This week should be different.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Bryce Young is coming off of one of the best games of his career as a Carolina Panther. He was comfortably above his career average in almost every statistic against the Chicago Bears, most notably with his 361 yards passing and three touchdowns. Panthers fans have long been asking for consistency from their young quarterback. Fortunately for them today, Young has only shown a modicum of consistently excellent play against one team: the Atlanta Falcons.

At first glance, it looks like the Panthers couldn’t have picked a better game than at Atlanta with which to bounce back from and build off of their Week 1 loss. Not only did Young appear to take a big step forward, but the defense in which they invested so much money in the offense gave up 59 points. You know, in case you hadn’t heard. Not only are they Young’s professional happy place, they are also starting third string quarterback Cooper Rush for the second week in a row. The defense will not likely get a better opportunity to clamp down on an uncomplicated passing game all season.

The only real threat that the Falcons are expected to field is Bijan Robinson. Carolina gave up 291 yards rushing and four rushing touchdowns between D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, and Caleb Williams. Robinson is a more talented runner than any of them. He will likely get his share of yards today, but should also provide an excellent test for whatever adjustments the staff wants to make the defense from last week. And that’s just what we’re predicting this week.

Staff predictions for Week 2

Walker Clement

Panthers 31, Falcons 17 – The Panthers give up 100 yards rushing to Robinson, but stifle Cooper Rush while Young and Brad Idzik keep their foot on the gas.

Jonathan DeLong

Panthers 27, Falcons 21 – Defense looks better against a much worse opposing offense and Bryce Young keeps up his dominance over the Falcons in their stadium.

Brian Beversluis

Panthers 17, Falcons 13 – Panthers narrowly beat the Falcons but Bijan Robinson runs all over them.

Daniel Belton

Panthers 24, Falcons 10 – The Panthers defense gets on track a bit against [Falcons QB], while Bryce and the offense only cool off a little. Panthers take control of the division with a victory.

Eric Buchanan

Panthers 29, Falcons 17 – Panthers Defense bounces back in a big way while Bryce Young continues to be the Falcons kryptonite.

These predictions average out to a comfortable 26-16 win for the Carolina Panthers, well above the current -2.5 point spread in favor of the Panthers over at FanDuel. That score has occurred 25 times in NFL history per nflscorigami.com and Pro Football Reference. The Carolina Panthers lost the last 26-16 game in the NFL to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4 of the 202 season. Frankie Luvu provided about as much offense as the rest of the Panthers team in a disappointing effort against Kyler Murray and Kliff Kingsbury’s final season together.

item.title: When will Shedeur Sanders start? Why Browns QB is backing up Deshaun Watson
item.description: Deshaun Watson beat Shedeur Sanders for the Browns' starting quarterback job, but the 2025 fifth-round pick could still challenge for playing time.
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns held what was viewed as a wide-open quarterback competition during the 2026 NFL offseason.

Ultimately, Deshaun Watson beat out Shedeur Sanders despite first-year Browns coach Todd Monken opining that Sanders had "closed the gap" during the competition.

"We felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that (Watson) was ahead of Shedeur," Monken explained at the time. "Shedeur's closed that gap, for sure. And that's a credit to him. We look forward to Shedeur continuing to grow as a player, but ultimately, we're about Week 1. Putting our best foot forward over the next three weeks."

Naturally, Monken's praise of Sanders created another question. When exactly would the Colorado product get a chance to start if things don't go well under Watson's leadership?

Here's what to know about Cleveland's timeline for playing Sanders during the 2026 NFL season.

When will Shedeur Sanders start?

The Browns haven't yet provided a clue about when Sanders might start. When announcing Watson as the starter, Monken said he didn't expect Cleveland's quarterback situation to change on a week-to-week basis.

"Ultimately we expect him to play well or we wouldn't be starting him," Monken said, referencing Watson.

That said, there has been plenty of speculation about Sanders being given a chance to start as early as Week 3, when the Browns make their 2026 home debut.

Watson has endured a rocky relationship with Browns fans across his time in Cleveland. He has routinely been booed for his poor performance across his tenure, including during his rough outing at Huntington Bank Field in preseason Week 2.

Watson jabbed at the fans for their reaction to him during that game, referring to the boos as "personal" and "disrespectful."

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson told reporters. "It’s a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing. I'm gonna keep whatever I feel with me and my family, internally, on how I feel about that and just move on."

Watson later apologized for his reaction to the fans after being named the team's No. 1 quarterback.

Nonetheless, the incident has only further fueled speculation that the Browns could install Sanders as the starter for the home opener if Watson doesn't perform well during Cleveland's season-opening road games.

Why isn't Shedeur Sanders starting?

As mentioned, Sanders isn't starting because the Browns named Watson their starting quarterback to open the 2026 NFL season.

Watson and Sanders were engaged in a tight quarterback battle throughout the offseason, and each got a chance to start one preseason game. Watson looked the better of the two quarterbacks in preseason Week 1, his start, while Sanders vastly outperformed Watson in Cleveland's second preseason game.

Many believed Sanders would get the nod after his strong performance against the Buffalo Bills. Instead, Monken backed Watson, noting he had remained slightly ahead of Sanders throughout the competition.

Watson finished the 2026 preseason completing 16 of 27 passes (59.3%) for 162 yards, no touchdowns and one interception. By comparison, Sanders completed 15 of 22 passes (68.2%) for 153 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

Deshaun Watson stats 2026

Watson started Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season for the Browns. Things didn't go well, as Cleveland's offense largely struggled to move the ball in a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Watson's overall numbers don't look too bad. He completed 16 of 22 passes for 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception while scrambling for 38 yards on six carries.

However, much of Watson's production came in garbage time, as Cleveland's lone touchdown came when the team was already down 34-3. He was also sacked five times and fumbled once across his outing.

Watson will look to post a better performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2. If he can't, he could soon find Sanders breathing down his neck in what figures to be a season-long quarterback battle.

item.title: Steelers vs Patriots live updates: TV info, live stream, odds for Week 2 game
item.description: Pittsburgh stole a 21-14 victory against the Patriots a year ago by generating five turnovers against quarterback Drake Maye and Co.
item.content:encoded:
For once, the Pittsburgh Steelers head to New England with some history on their side.

They'll face the Patriots in an NFL Week 2 matchup Sunday following a victory at Gillette Stadium a year ago in which the defense forced five turnovers to secure a 21-14 Week 3 victory. It was Pittsburgh's first win in Foxboro, Mass., since a 2011 triumph. The Steelers had dropped decisions in each of their past four visits and had dropped eight of their last nine against their AFC nemesis overall.

Coach Mike Vrabel, quarterback Drake Maye and Co. ultimately got the last laugh by reaching the Super Bowl as AFC champions. At least for an afternoon, however, they didn't have many answers for the playmaking of the Steelers defense.

Required reading: Grading the Steelers' NFL Week 1 win: T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith were disruptive

Maye threw an interception and lost a fourth-quarter fumble that short-circuited any hopes of a comeback. Rhamondre Stevenson lost two fumbles and Antonio Gibson lost one earlier in the game. T.J. Watt and the Steelers defense will look to be similarly opportunistic this week after generating a pair of turnovers -- including a interception returned for a touchdown -- in a Week 1 win against Atlanta.

Offensively, Aaron Rodgers and the offense will look to improve on an effort that was barely good enough to take advantage of New England's miscues last year. The veteran quarterback managed just 139 yards through the air, while the running game averaged just 2.5 yards per carry en route to totaling 64 for the afternoon.

New England dropped the NFL season opener at Seattle last week. Maye has had more than a week to think about his three interceptions in that game, so it will be interesting to see whether he plays a tighter game or struggles the way he did when Pittsburgh was last in town.

Getting beaten off the line of scrimmage repeatedly and not adding much as a run blocker puts them at a disadvantage at a time when the offense is looking for any advantage to capitalize on.
